Coverage is evaluated against the tuple Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T): the workspace W, the governed outcome G, the exact basis B, the known evaluation inventory E, the declared frame set S and the time or immutable checkpoint T of the claim. Changing any material member may invalidate the coverage result.
P3, P6

The ledger holds at least, for each evaluation: evaluation (the exact question or predicate); provenance (the source establishing materiality); subject and basis (the exact workspace coordinate); selected frames (the frames capable of evaluating it); actor envelope (the competence and context required); semantic authority (the owner of the evaluated meaning); operation authority (the existing owner grant where the evaluation performs a construction, transformation, admission, publication or mutation; otherwise none); decision authority (the owner of the disposition); evidence (the required observations and their provenance); dependencies (material frame or seam relations); status (the coverage disposition); residual (uncertainty, exclusion or re-entry condition).
P4b, P6
The baseline coverage statuses are covered, separately_covered, conditionally_covered, conflicted, uncovered, unknown and excluded_by_authority.
P4b, P6

Coverage stays falsifiable and externally challengeable. Challenge sources include human knowledge outside the current frame set; independent review; historical failures and predecessor systems; mutation, adversarial and counterexample search; live operation and user behaviour; adjacent workspace or domain comparison; and changes in actor capability, law, dependencies or topology. The method requires an explicit residual boundary and never a claim of metaphysical or universal completeness.

A declared decision rule consumes closed frame results. The rule states which results are mandatory; how conflict and indeterminacy are handled; which basis relations must agree; which decision authority owns the conjunction; and whether any result may veto or defer the decision.
P6, P4a

Diagnosis asks, in this order: 1 Was the correct declared frame activated? 2 Were the subject and basis exact? 3 Was the actor inside the capability envelope? 4 Was admissible evidence available? 5 Is a material variable or invariant missing from the frame? 6 Is a required conjunction or translation missing? 7 Is the evaluation family itself wrong or incomplete? 8 Is another frame required? The order prevents every difficult evaluation from creating another frame.
P2
A composite with a known failure or an uncovered required obligation cannot project success; a known failure A and an uncovered obligation B survive every join.

Human authority may declare an initial project frame set from accumulated practice, known failure modes, domain expertise, the outcome's risk and knowledge of the available actors, without reconstructing it from the workspace bottom up. The declaration records: the governed workspace and outcome; the known evaluation inventory; the selected frames and their capability envelopes; intentional overlaps and separately activated checks; known frame dependencies or translations; semantic, evaluation, operation where material, decision and acceptance authority; known exclusions and residual uncertainty; and the conditions for revision.
P6, P2

The coverage evaluator derives the known evaluation inventory from every material available source, including where applicable: goals, intent, product definition, requirements and accepted method; accepted design, its ontology, identities, lifecycles, authorities and algorithms; implementation capabilities and externally observable behaviour; operational, release, security, safety and governance obligations; dependencies and interaction seams; evidence, tests, scenarios, qualification and acceptance claims; historical tickets, check-ins, commentary, post-mortems, incidents and rejected candidates; days-long loops, resets, repeated repairs and discovered rival paths; known agent capability limits and prior invisible violations; and applicable external law, contracts or standards. The inventory records provenance and materiality.
P2, P6

Every mandatory constraint is satisfied with valid applicable evidence. Common agreement cannot discard a constraint or a material counterexample that only one contributor found. A missing, wrong-subject, conflicted or indeterminate mandatory result stays unresolved under the declared rule; aggregate green status cannot replace it.
P4b, P5
Every material revision changes frame identity or revision coordinates and states which prior activations, results and coverage claims require reevaluation.
P3, P4b

These observations trigger frame diagnosis: a competent actor repeatedly cannot see a known material violation; a local repair creates or duplicates another authority path; work repeatedly resets after apparently valid local completion; long implementation loops produce no stable closure; proof passes while the claimed outcome stays unbound; a material failure is visible only after broad integration; reviewers repeatedly expand context without reaching a decidable question; two actors use the same frame name but evaluate different material relations; or a topology mutation leaves prior verdicts apparently current.
P4b, P5

Question 1 is answered by family inclusion, not by set membership. An evaluation is within a frame's family when the question it decides is one the frame's declared evaluation family states, at the frame's declared coordinates. Membership of the frame in the frame set, the frame's name, a role label or similar wording of the question does not place an evaluation in the frame's family; an activation of a frame on an evaluation outside its family answers question 1 no, whatever the frame's standing in the set.
P2, P1; RF-001; the material relation drawn is evaluation-to-family inclusion; rc.2 #diagnostic-order, #evaluation, #rf-001-evaluation-relativity, #applicability-and-required-results

A revision may: clarify activation or evidence acquisition; change the capability envelope; add or remove a material relation; split an overloaded frame; merge duplicative frames where capability and authority stay sound; add intentional overlap; add or revise a conjunction or translation; retire a frame whose evaluation family is no longer material; or revise the project evaluation inventory.
P4b

Stated plainly: a material revision of a frame produces a new frame revision coordinate. Every prior closed result bound to the previous revision of a materially revised frame is bound to a mismatched coordinate (RF-005) and is invalidated for reuse until it is re-checked against the new revision. The revision record lists those results as reopened; a result leaves that list only by a recorded re-check that finds it demonstrably independent of the change, or by re-evaluation on the new revision. A material revision does not select which of the results bound to the prior revision it reopens, and silence does not keep a result closed. A non-material revision, for example one that clarifies an activation or acquires evidence without changing any declaration, produces no new coordinate and reopens no result; the revision record states that the revision is non-material.
P3, P4b; RF-005, RF-011, ACTIVATION section 7; rc.2 #revision-actions, #rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates, #return-a-closed-result

symbols.label: Activated frame: one frame declaration bound to an exact evaluation, workspace subject, basis, actor and evidence-acquisition boundary; a reusable declaration is not evidence that a particular activation was correct
Applicability: the determination, from the owning evaluation and scope declarations and sufficient basis-bound facts, of which frame obligations apply to the exact subject

Basis: the exact state a step, claim, result or evaluation binds: every version, identity, time, topology, authority, configuration or evidence coordinate whose change can alter it; immutable, or moving with a declared way of detecting advancement and a declared reevaluation condition; mixed bases need an explicit composite relation
Claim: an assertion with subject, property, basis, witness relation and falsifier

Closed result: identifies the frame and its activation, the subject, the basis, the evaluation, the actor, the evidence, the verdict, the residual uncertainty and the invalidation conditions; minimal shape REFERENCE_FRAME section 13; available for reuse under an applicability check

Completeness boundary: without an independently established closed-domain completeness predicate, a finite frame set cannot establish the absence of undiscovered material evaluations from its own inventory

Coordinate: the complete local position from which a value, event, decision, observation or action is interpreted (basis, identity, lineage, input, evidence, authority); equal names, values, shapes or apparent positions do not establish coordinate equality, which follows a declared relation
Required obligation set R, admitted coverage C and uncovered coverage R minus C

Coverage ledger: one row per evaluation holding at least evaluation, provenance, subject and basis, selected frames, actor envelope, semantic authority, operation authority, decision authority, evidence, dependencies, status and residual
Coverage status: covered, separately_covered, conditionally_covered, conflicted, uncovered, unknown or excluded_by_authority
Coverage tuple Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T): workspace, governed outcome, exact basis, known evaluation inventory, declared frame set, and the time or immutable checkpoint of the claim
Decision authority: the role permitted to accept, reject or otherwise dispose a result

Decision rule: states which results are mandatory, how conflict and indeterminacy are handled, which basis relations must agree, which decision authority owns the conjunction, and whether any result may veto or defer
Diagnostic order: the eight questions asked in order before another frame is created
Evaluation family: evaluations that need the same material-relation manifold, authority basis and result algebra; similar wording proves no shared family
Evaluation inventory: the known material evaluations of a workspace and outcome, derived from every material available source, with provenance and materiality recorded

Frame set: the human-declared family of frames available for a governed outcome or workspace; may hold overlaps, alternatives, specialist, exploratory and separately activated assurance frames; not required to be a partition, tree, stack or exhaustive ontology
Frame-set authority: the human authority that declares or accepts a project frame set

Frame-set declaration: the human-declared record of workspace and outcome, evaluation inventory, selected frames and envelopes, overlaps, dependencies and translations, authorities, exclusions and residual uncertainty, and revision conditions
Method function revise(frame_set, new_evidence, failures, capability_change, topology_change) -> proposed_frame_set_delta; section 10
Invalidator: a changed material input, basis or declared revising observation that invalidates a result before reliance
Missing-frame signal: an observation that triggers frame diagnosis
Operation authority: the owner-issued grant to construct, transform, admit, publish or mutate a material subject where an evaluation performs such an operation; a read-only evaluation declares none
invalid_basis: the subject or basis cannot support the evaluation

Reference frame: a finite specification of the attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations required to perform one declared evaluation family over a stated basis; its components are the frame tuple
The one core result algebra for every evaluation and stop state
Result conjunction: a declared decision rule consumes closed frame results
Revision action: a lawful change to a frame set in response to evidence, failure, capability change or topology change
RF-001 Evaluation relativity: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-005 Exact basis and coordinates: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-011 Topology mutation and recharting: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
Semantic authority: the owner of meaning for a material relation

Topology: the relation structure among material entities, capabilities, authorities, lifecycle state spaces, adjacencies and seams visible to a frame at one basis; a transition that changes any of them is a topology mutation that may invalidate the frame's coordinates
